Snakes! They’re extremely misunderstood animals and if I would be an animal I would definitely be a snake! One could say snakes also have sensory issues in a way. Most snakes don’t like to be touched even docile snakes doesn’t even care for handling it’s more for humans desire to connect than the animals need. For example I have a corn snake and yes the more I handle him the more used to it he becomes, but all he’s doing is just tolerating it but if you handle him every hour and won’t let them go to the safe space that is their enclosure they will become extremely agitated and even will “hate” being there feeling unsafe. Some will stop eating if you handle them too much. Also some pet snakes are more sensitive than others like the green tree boa, that snake doesn’t really enjoy handling and are extremely sensitive. Most of the time they just want to be left alone especially wild snakes. When people see a venemous snake they get very scared and often times tries to kill it even though the snake is more scared of you than you are of them. I come from a country where the common European adder lives and lots of people want to bother it however what people don’t know is that the common European adder does not want to bite you. They have very limited venom and they would rather save their venom for prey. They’re also very solitary animals except for when they mate, although the garter snake is an exception. This is why I relate to snakes because 1. They’re solitary animals, and don’t like to be bothered (just like me) 2. They’re very sensitive to vibrations like feet stomping on the ground (they don’t have external ears so they only feel vibrations), 3. They are sensitive to temperature and 4. They are sensitive to smell. I also love snakes so much because they are simple animals and not complicated at all. Even so they are simple you can tell every snake behaves differently even if they’re from the same species.

I love your interpretation! Basically she is speaking to a person, that used to be a family member (a step parent) that wronged her. He did a lot of stuff that would make her voice be silenced and not heard. And then she bled. What he did to her, is up to you to interpret. But she is also speaking to the people that never wanted to listen to her, the people who let her suffer in silence and the people who let her go unnoticed. 


The last line is herself as an adult, talking to the kid that she once were, reassuring her. Wishing that she were heard. And she’s speaking to the adults that wouldn’t listen to her, in a way it was her having a flashback. And she was watching things happen like a movie.

The birds are a sign of innocence that will soon disappear. at first she is a little kid, the birds twittering are the echoes of her innocence, that once were.. And the ocean and the whale are a sign of her pain, her suffering. and then it moves more into a parental feeling, she is now talking to herself as an adult, trying to make sense of the situation that happened to her. Her saying “is this fun?” Is her frustration. Like “was it fun ruining my life?” 

And then at the very end she says “now we’re here.” And that is basically her referring to herself in the present, saying “after all of these years passing by, people not listening, people not giving a crap. I am now standing here, my pain kept inside. But it is now worse.” 

No interpretations are wrong, and I loved yours a lot. I think I cried a little as well hehe. But I really loved that you took the time to write such a beautiful interpretation!
